application_niche: Lightweight aerospace structural intermetallic & oxidation-resistant Ti-alloy reinforcement
verdict_comment: Extremely practical. Built entirely from cheap, earth-abundant metals (Ti, Al, Cu), it sits -35.8 meV/atom below the hull (deepest of all 14 winners), is intrinsically ductile (B0/G = 1.98, nu = 0.284), lightweight (4.20 g/cm^3), and 53% stiffer per unit mass than Ti-6Al-4V (E/rho = 39.4 vs 25.7 GPa*cm^3/g). Congruent arc-melting / induction-melting compatible.

application_niche: Ultra-dense radiation-shielding / high-temperature nuclear control-rod cermet
verdict_comment: Mechanically outstanding (B0 = 262 GPa, G = 153 GPa, H_V = 22.0 GPa, deep hull -32.1 meV/at), but Lutetium (~$2,900/kg) makes bulk structural use uneconomical. Useful only in high-value nuclear/neutron-absorbing or extreme-environment aerospace nozzle inserts; for bulk use, substitute Zr3(MnB3)2 or Nb3(NiB3)2.

application_niche: Accident-tolerant nuclear fuel cladding, hypersonic leading-edge coating & wear-resistant tooling
verdict_comment: Highly practical and earth-abundant (Zr, Cr, B). Deep thermodynamic stability (-25.9 meV/at), exceptionally clean phonon spectrum (lowest optical mode 5.78 THz), ductile (B0/G = 2.01), high fracture toughness (K_Ic = 4.6 MPa*m^0.5), and strong corrosion/oxidation resistance from Cr + Zr.

usefulness_rating: SCIENTIFIC / ULTRA-NICHE CATALYSIS ONLY (Prohibitive Ir Cost)
cost_tier: Extremely High (~$118,000/kg due to 76 wt% Ir)
application_niche: Thin-film electrocatalyst (OER/HER) or ultra-high-temperature spark-plug / thruster tip coating
verdict_comment: Exceptionally ductile for a refractory boride (B0/G = 2.97, nu = 0.349, B0 = 283 GPa) with strong QE-PBE stability (-0.687 eV/at), but Iridium (~$155,000/kg) rules out any bulk structural application. Only viable as a sub-micron thin-film coating or noble-metal electrocatalyst.

usefulness_rating: HIGHLY USEFUL (Top Superalloy & Cutting-Tool Cermet Winner)
application_niche: Ductile MAB-like refractory cermet for turbine blades, hot-working dies & cutting tools
verdict_comment: One of the best all-around engineering discoveries in the campaign. Combines ceramic-like stiffness (E = 395 GPa, B0 = 280 GPa, G = 156 GPa, H_V = 21.1 GPa, Debye T = 722 K) with metallic ductility (B0/G = 1.79 > 1.75 threshold, K_Ic = 5.4 MPa*m^0.5) using standard industrial metals (Nb, Ni, B).

usefulness_rating: NICHE ULTRA-INCOMPRESSIBLE ANVIL / COATING (Ir Cost Limited)
cost_tier: Very High (~$52,000/kg due to 33 wt% Ir)
application_niche: High-pressure diamond-anvil gasket / ultra-incompressible electrical contact coating
verdict_comment: Highest bulk modulus of all 14 winners (B0 = 326.4 GPa, E = 363 GPa) while remaining highly ductile (B0/G = 2.36, nu = 0.314). Bulk use is prevented by Iridium cost and high density (15.05 g/cm^3), making it a specialty high-pressure anvil or thin-film contact material.

application_niche: Lightweight automotive pistons, EV battery enclosures & cast Al-Si-Ni structural precipitate phase
verdict_comment: Immediately useful and dirt-cheap (Al, Si, Ni). At rho = 3.21 g/cm^3, it delivers E/rho = 33.9 GPa*cm^3/g (+33% stiffer per kg than Al-7075 and Ti-6Al-4V) while remaining ductile (B0/G = 2.15, nu = 0.299). Can be synthesized directly in standard aluminum foundries.

application_niche: Damage-tolerant MAX-phase coating, fusion/fission reactor first-wall armor & high-T heating elements
verdict_comment: A standout industrial winner. Hexagonal P6_3/mmc MAX-type layered carbo-silicide with 1.1 meV/atom agreement between MACE and Quantum ESPRESSO PBE (-0.550 vs -0.551 eV/at). Lightweight (4.55 g/cm^3), very high specific stiffness (E/rho = 51.4 GPa*cm^3/g, 2x Ti-6Al-4V), and extraordinarily ductile (B0/G = 2.44) for a carbide.

application_niche: High-hardness wear plates, hypersonic thermal-protection struts & cutting-tool inserts
verdict_comment: Strongest QE-PBE formation enthalpy of the entire set (-0.822 eV/atom) and near-zero DFT stress (+0.12 GPa). Uses cheap, abundant elements (Zr, Mn, B) to achieve E/rho = 57.4 GPa*cm^3/g (+123% over Ti-6Al-4V) and high Vickers hardness (H_V = 23.9 GPa). Slightly on the brittle side (B0/G = 1.54), best used in cermet composites.

usefulness_rating: SCIENTIFIC / QUANTUM MATERIALS INTEREST ONLY (Ir Cost)
cost_tier: Extremely High (~$119,000/kg due to 76 wt% Ir)
verdict_comment: Very ductile (B0/G = 3.02, nu = 0.351) with strong 5d spin-orbit coupling on the Ir kagome/honeycomb network, making it interesting for condensed-matter physics (superconductivity/SOC), but completely impractical for structural engineering.

usefulness_rating: MODERATE / SPECIALTY AEROSPACE (Highest Specific Stiffness, Sc Cost Limited)
application_niche: Ultra-lightweight satellite / precision aerospace stiffness-critical struts
verdict_comment: Delivers the highest specific stiffness of all 14 winners (E/rho = 59.3 GPa*cm^3/g at rho = 4.49 g/cm^3, +131% over Ti-6Al-4V, Debye T = 742 K) with ductile-borderline mechanics (B0/G = 1.74). Scandium cost limits it to high-end aerospace/defense hardware unless Sc supply expands.

usefulness_rating: SCIENTIFIC / ULTRA-HARD NOBLE BORIDE BENCHMARK ONLY (Os + Sc Cost)
cost_tier: Extremely High (~$11,500/kg due to Os + Sc)
application_niche: Academic benchmark for 5d noble-metal tetragonal borides
verdict_comment: Thermodynamically and dynamically stable ductile 5d boride (B0 = 259 GPa, B0/G = 2.47), but Osmium toxicity (OsO4 volatility at high T) and extreme cost ($13,000/kg) make it unsuitable for practical engineering.

application_niche: Ultra-high-temperature hot-pressing dies, crucible linings & erosion-resistant turbine coatings
verdict_comment: Isostructural to Nb3(NiB3)2 with even higher bulk modulus (B0 = 288 GPa, G = 150 GPa, E = 383 GPa) and true intrinsic ductility (B0/G = 1.92, K_Ic = 5.4 MPa*m^0.5). Tantalum is pricier and heavier than Niobium, so Nb3(NiB3)2 is preferred for weight-sensitive parts while Ta3(NiB3)2 excels in extreme thermal/corrosive environments.

application_niche: High-temperature refractory structural boride & liquid-metal / molten-salt compatible armor
verdict_comment: Very practical Ni-free refractory boride built from Nb, Mo, and B. High bulk modulus (B0 = 296 GPa, second highest overall), strongly ductile (B0/G = 2.14, nu = 0.298, K_Ic = 5.2 MPa*m^0.5), high specific stiffness (E/rho = 46.8 GPa*cm^3/g), and avoids Ni activation in nuclear environments.
